purpose: Final reciprocal-coverage batches needed before v1 insight mining. These batches were selected by source stratum, not premise-map graph shape.

batches.stratum: workflow execution and evidence lifecycle semantics
batches.selectionRule: Read the maintained workflow authority as an execution/evidence system rather than as experiment content.

sources.notes: Workflow success is separated from scientific outcome; timeout from completed-negative; failed/cancelled runs may still contain valid completed evidence; immutable SHA, population identity, provenance and retention semantics are explicit. These are already covered by treatment-delivery, observability, censoring, evidence-state, authority and information-lifetime premises.

batches.result: No new parent. Workflow lifecycle semantics converge with v1 epistemic and execution premises.

batches.stratum: dated report spot checks against current synthesis authorities
batches.selectionRule: One population/evidence report and one whole-system audit were selected before reading their premise implications, to test whether synthesis documents had erased decision-bearing concepts.

sources.notes: The report independently reinforces effective independence, claim-relative population role, treatment-lineage exposure, temporal corpus identity, and the fact that a population can become development evidence after influencing redesign. It adds no new parent beyond B001 candidates.

Identity drift, fallback/treatment ambiguity, stage participation, budget displacement, continuation lifetime, provenance authentication, tri-state evidence, benchmark censoring and research-data reuse are all represented by v1 or the post-v1 epistemic candidates already found.

batches.result: Historical report detail did not expose a new parent after the epistemic additions; this is a meaningful anti-summary-loss saturation signal.

batches.stratum: current research authorities outside the obvious premise-map source core
batches.selectionRule: Current methodological/resource documents selected because they can affect experimental conclusions despite not being solver mechanisms.

sources.notes: Exposes opportunity population as the causal denominator for detectability. This is retained as a specialization rather than a new parent.
Population locking, selection timing, outcome conditioning, replay identity and claim scope converge with existing population/evidence premises.
Reachability ambiguity and bounded epistemic stop conditions are already represented by source presence, first-loss, causal residual and maturity/evidence premises.

batches.result: One useful detectability specialization, no new parent.

batches.selectionRule: Three deliberately heterogeneous sources: mutable runtime storage, offline labelled-state replay, and default-off mechanism disposition. Chosen to maximize conceptual distance from each other and from B001.

sources.notes: Physical persistence versus semantic persistence, cross-attempt state history, cache warmth, ownership scope and concurrency all fit state-sufficiency, observability and information-lifetime premises.
Witness identity, abstention, supported-population coverage, selection/search-on-atlas disclosure, soundness authority and replay-to-production maturity are all represented.
Code retention is explicitly separated from promotion evidence; reopen conditions and mechanism/form scope converge with v1 evidence-state and maturity premises.

batches.result: Final heterogeneous batch produced no new parent, scope split, specialization, or ontology escape. Together with B008, this satisfies the predeclared two-batch no-high-impact-new-parent saturation condition.

residualUncertainty: No finite archaeology can establish absence of undocumented or never-articulated premises.
Representative runtime-code sampling is not exhaustive line-by-line code proof.
The map remains historically conditioned by the solver and research apparatus that produced the repository.
Future architectures can create premise categories that have no clean ancestor in v1.
